summary:
The title of the proposed bill is the Human Trafficking and Transportation (Control) (First Amendment) Bill, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to protect the self-respect, freedom, and fundamental rights of persons affected by human trafficking spread as an organized crime, ensure access to justice for victims at high risk or subjected to trafficking and transportation, bring persons accused of human trafficking offences domestically or abroad under the legal framework, broaden the scope of penalties, and make all three levels of government accountable (Statement of Objects and Reasons). This Act shall come into force immediately upon authentication (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The federal government shall arrange monitoring at international borders, international airports, and potential trafficking sites for the prevention and control of human trafficking and transportation (Section 27A, Subsection 1, Page 7). The Nepal Government shall send back rescued foreign citizens through diplomatic channels (Section 12, Subsection 4, Page 3). The Ministry may issue guidelines or standards as necessary subject to the Act or Rules (Section 29A, Page 7). A Provincial Committee chaired by the Secretary overseeing human trafficking control shall be formed in every province to coordinate between provincial government bodies and non-governmental organizations, and its formation and operation shall be as provided in provincial law or provincial gazette notice (Section 23A, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 6). A Local Committee chaired by the Rural Executive Chairperson/Vice-Chairperson or Municipal Executive Mayor/Deputy Mayor shall be formed in every local level for local coordination, and its formation and operation shall be as provided in local law or local gazette notice (Section 23B, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 6). A District Committee shall be formed in every district, which shall coordinate with the National Committee for the rehabilitation of victims rescued within Nepal (Section 23, Subsection 1, Page 6 and Section 12, Subsection 1, Page 3).

The police office registering a complaint must keep confidential the complainant's name, surname, address, and identifying details (Section 5, Subsection 2, Page 2). A center keeping victims under protection must keep confidential the victim's name, surname, address, identifying details, and related records (Section 20A, Subsection 1, Page 5). No person shall print, broadcast, or publicly disclose through newspapers or other media the real name, photo, or details adverse to the character of a victim without consent, and consent given by a child shall not be considered consent for this purpose (Section 25, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 6). Deadlines applying to these entities and institutions are not stated in the bill.

This bill provides for forming Provincial Committees at the provincial level and Local Committees at the local level, and mandates a District Committee in every district (Section 23, Section 23A, and Section 23B, Page 6). The main functions of these committees are to control human trafficking and transportation offences and coordinate between government and non-governmental bodies regarding victim rescue and rehabilitation (Section 23A, Subsection 1 and Section 23B, Subsection 1, Page 6). The Provincial Committee is chaired by the Secretary overseeing human trafficking control, and the Local Committee is chaired by the Rural Executive Chairperson/Vice-Chairperson or Municipal Executive Mayor/Deputy Mayor (Section 23A, Subsection 1 and Section 23B, Subsection 1, Page 6). Provisions regarding a chief executive are not stated in the bill. A Rehabilitation Fund shall be maintained to rescue, repatriate, and rehabilitate victims and assist in operating rehabilitation centers, which shall also bear rescue expenses for Nepali citizens trafficked abroad (Section 14, Subsection 1, Page 4 and Section 12, Subsection 7, Page 3).

A person buying or selling a human shall be punished with 20 years imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 4 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 4). A person forcing someone into prostitution with or without taking benefit shall be punished, depending on the degree of the offence, with imprisonment from 10 years to 15 years and a fine from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause b, Page 4). A person removing a human organ except as provided by prevailing law shall be punished with 10 years imprisonment and a fine from Rs. 4 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause c, Page 4). A person engaging in prostitution shall be punished with imprisonment from 2 months to 6 months and a fine from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 1 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause d, Page 4). A person taking a human abroad or bringing a human from abroad for buying, selling, or forcing into prostitution shall be punished with imprisonment from 10 years to 15 years and a fine from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh, and if taking or bringing a child, with imprisonment from 15 years to 20 years and a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 4 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause e, Subclause 1, Page 4). A person taking a human from one place to another within Nepal for buying, selling, or forcing into prostitution shall be punished with imprisonment from 5 years to 10 years and a fine from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh, and if taking a child, with imprisonment from 10 years to 12 years and a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 3 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause e, Subclause 2, Page 4). A person taking a human from one place to another within Nepal under Clause b of Subsection 2 of Section 4 for exploitation shall be punished with imprisonment from 1 year to 2 years and a fine from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 1 lakh, and if taken abroad, with imprisonment from 2 years to 5 years and a fine from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh (Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause f, Page 4).
